Opinions split on the sweet spot and spin, as Otro Nivel / Justpadel finds a very big sweet spot and a lot of spin, while the4Set finds the sweet spot smaller than the Neuron Edge and the glossy surface harder for spin shots. Weight and demands are the other catch, since Otro Nivel / Justpadel calls it heavy at 365 to 375 g and Padel Racket Australia says late or off-center contact is punished.

highlights.text: glossy surface harder for spin shots

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the control, manoeuvrability and secure volleys, and suit it to players who build points rather than rely on power. Spin is where they split: Padel Review scores it 6.5 and dislikes the lack of spin, while Fabio Ferro scores spin 8.5. Several reviewers, including Extreme Padel and Probando Palas, point players wanting more power to the Neuron 02 Edge, and Fabio Ferro calls the 319 euro price high.

highlights.text: more power to the Neuron 02 Edge

paras: Reviewers praise the HRD+ for smash power and stable volley blocks, and rate it for advanced attacking players, with some saying it fits the left side best. Opinions split on handling and forgiveness: Simone Mazzola Padel finds defence better than expected with a good sweet spot, while Extreme Padel finds it more demanding than the standard Metalbone and Tom Pandore says it left them late on fast balls. Hotel Palas picks it over the standard 3.5 for control on blocks, and several reviewers prefer it with the weights removed.

highlights.text: more demanding than the standard Metalbone

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the spin from the rough texture and the easy handling for a diamond shape, and place it with advanced or aggressive players, often on the left side. Power is where takes split: Padel5 finds smashes go like a cannon, while Simone Mazzola Padel and Padel Review find the power less extreme than expected. Mejora Tu Padel and the4Set are mixed, with Mejora Tu Padel seeing little difference from the regular Defy and the ball rising in defense, and the4Set struggling to feel the ball on lobs.

highlights.text: easy handling for a diamond shape
the power less extreme than expected
struggling to feel the ball on lobs

paras: Reviewers who liked it, mostly advanced and intermediate-high players who want power, praise the dry touch and the easy handling for an offensive racket at roughly 360 to 366 g. Mixed takes come from the Soft name: Mejora Tu Padel calls it a hard racket that is only a little more flexible than the standard 3.0, and Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel finds it only slightly more forgiving than the regular Viper, while pdhsports finds it much softer than the older Technical range. Dani 13 says off-centre balls die, and the4Set reports less control at high speed and on volleys than the hard version.

highlights.text: easy handling for an offensive racket

paras: Reviewers mostly praise strong power on smashes and fast attacking shots, and say it suits experienced or advanced players with good physical condition. Reported weights range from 366 g to 378 g, and reviewers describe it as heavy and hard to handle, with a small sweet spot and little ball output. Dani 13 rates control as very good, while Mejora Tu Padel finds low volleys float in transition play, and Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel prefers the Soft version in defence.

Reviewers mostly praise its control and easy handling, and it suits players who want a dry, predictable feel and build points rather than finish them. Sweet spot size is where opinions split: Simone Mazzola Padel finds the sweet spot not generous and the racket demanding, while Nico Ballesteros rates it as huge and forgiving compared with the Attack version. Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel finds it the stiffest and driest next to the AT10 12K and AT10 18K and harder on the arm, and Extreme Padel and el4Set both place its power below the Attack or the Genius 12K.

Reviewers praise the Endure V1 as a balanced round racket with good control and precision, suited to intermediate players and to those moving up to a first advanced racket. Mixed takes come mostly from comparisons with the Pro: Mejora Tu Padel finds it more manoeuvrable but with less body, and Justpadel finds smashes can kick out and would pick the Pro for power. Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel names it the most balanced of the three Endure models, though it is only correct on smashes.

Reviewers mostly praise it as a middle step between the Coello Pro and the Coello Team, with power that is easier to handle than the Pro, and some aim it at intermediate to advanced players. Simone Mazzola Padel finds it a softer Pro that is not different enough to justify a separate model, and calls it demanding to move at the net. Extreme Padel calls it head heavy with a reduced sweet spot, and Tino finds the sweet spot smaller and limits sessions to two hours.

highlights.text: easier to handle than the Pro
demanding to move at the net
head heavy with a reduced sweet spot

paras: Reviewers mostly describe an attacking diamond racket for intermediate to advanced players, praising its control at pace, viper shots and volleys. Opinions split on how it compares with other rackets: Peter Consuegra finds it clearly behind the Vertex 04 for control, while Rodri Ovide switched from the Vertex to the Hack. Sweet spot size also varies, with Padel Test by Roberto Cardi finding it high and not very wide, and Padel Review finding it bigger than on previous Hacks.

Reviewers praise the grip on the ball and spin from the 3D sandy surface, along with a wide sweet spot, for intermediate to advanced players. Sweet spot opinions differ: Extreme Padel finds it restricted and vibrating off centre, while Mejora Tu Padel calls it very wide. Padel Vlog Italia finds it more playable than the V2 and V2.5, but Padel Review prefers the older 2.5 and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi gives only 5.5 out of 10 for value at 310 euros.

Reviewers praise the soft, precise touch and the side weights that shift the balance between control and power. Simone Mazzola Padel calls it a builder's racket rather than a finisher and rates the 400 euro list price as very high, while Otro Nivel Padel finds it less powerful on the kick smash and heavier in defense than the Arrow Hit Control, though softer and less trampoline than the Metalbone Control. Padel House finds ball speed comes easily and recommends it to players with good technique, but warns that forcing the shot at the net can cost control.

highlights.text: side weights that shift the balance
forcing the shot at the net can cost control

paras: Reviewers recommend it mainly to intermediate and advanced players who like to attack, praising smash and viper power, with Padel Review and Practica Padel Team also noting no arm vibration. Takes split on handling: Conect Padel finds it more manoeuvrable in defence than expected and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi finds it easier than the Metalbone HRD, while Dani 13 finds handling worse than last year and Fabio Ferro finds it head-heavy and tiring. Several reviewers, including Padel Review and Practica Padel Team, find the sweet spot small and call the removable weight system too complicated, so both advise playing without weights.

Reviewers mostly praise the control and quick handling, and several recommend it to intermediate players who want a controlled, flat game, with Conect Padel calling it very recommendable for defensive players. Sweet spot opinions differ: PadelHQ calls it generous, while Dani 13 says off-center hits feel dry and Hotel Palas finds it narrower than the standard Metalbone CTRL, which it split two to two in a head to head. Power is the common limit, as Padel Review finds power drops as pace rises and Practica Padel Team scores smashes 6 out of 10.

Reviewers praise the large sweet spot and soft, comfortable feel, and Otro Nivel Padel calls it one of the best round rackets on the market, suited to intermediate and pro players. Power is where takes split: Tino finds it a bit too safe at the net and points to the standard Metalbone for explosive attacks, while Dani 13 calls it the most powerful control shape at this hardness but finds the volley zone slower with the Weight and Balance screws. Otro Nivel Padel also finds the Metalbone and Metalbone Hard more powerful, though with a smaller sweet spot.

highlights.text: a bit too safe at the net

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the round Metalbone CTRL 3.4 for a wide, central sweet spot, easy handling and comfort, with some noting no vibration. Mixed takes come from power and price: Dani 13 finds it bouncy at fast pace and well behind the normal Metalbone and Hard for flat smashes, Padel Review finds flat smashes lack punch, and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi calls the 379 euro list price too high. Fabio Ferro rates it easier to play than the 3.4 HRD but still prefers the HRD overall, while PadelCritic gives control as its best trait.

Reviewers mostly praise the power, with smashes, volleys and spin mentioned often, and most see it as suited to advanced players, particularly left-side players. Fabio Ferro and Practica Padel Team both find it more solid and powerful than the softer 3.4, though heavier in the head and harder to control. Opinions on the sweet spot differ, as Talk About Padel finds it big while Padel Review finds it smaller than the standard 3.4, and quoted prices run from about 350 to 490 €.

Reviewers praise the light, quick handling and a wider sweet spot than earlier Air Vipers, with good spin from the sandy rough surface. Opinions differ on power: Simone Mazzola Padel finds overhead power lacking at the low weight, while PadelVergleich calls the power impressive but the sweet spot still small. Padel Lovers and Fabio Ferro both prefer it to the Technical Viper 2025, though Padel Lovers warns that weaker technique can still bring short balls.

Reviewers praise the Air Viper 2026 for easy movement and quick net play, and some find it more comfortable and slightly more elastic than the 2025 model. Fabio Ferro finds less control and a late ball exit on volleys when forced, while Padelful warns that the sweet spot is demanding and Max Streltcoff / padel.how calls it medium. Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel finds it less dry than older versions, and Simone Mazzola Padel sees the sandblasted roughness as a step back from last year.

highlights.text: easy movement and quick net play

paras: Reviewers praise the control, wide sweet spot and spin, and Padel Review and El chini consejo place it with intermediate to advanced players. Feel is where takes differ: El chini consejo finds it harder than the Vertex, Metalbone HRD and AT10 18K Genius, while Probando Palas calls it medium-hard and about half a point harder than the AT10 12K. Padel Review finds 372 g less maneuverable, and Fabio Ferro notes less raw power than the Technical Viper.

highlights.text: control, wide sweet spot and spin
less raw power than the Technical Viper

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a round control racket for upper-intermediate to advanced players, with stable defence, controlled bandeja and vibora, and a large sweet spot. Dani 13 finds the centred sweet spot slightly smaller and the handling demanding, while Fabio Ferro calls the sweet spot bigger and the feel a little less dry than the 2025 model. Simone Mazzola Padel warns the hard feel is rough on the arm, whereas CONSIGN 77 recommends it to players prone to arm fatigue, and Pádel con Clase sees little change from the 2024 and no extra power.

highlights.text: hard feel is rough on the arm

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the smash and flat-shot power and suit the racket to advanced, aggressive players who bring their own technique. Opinions split on the sweet spot, as PADELARTE calls it wide for an attacking racket while Fabio Ferro rates it the smallest of the Viper sisters. Padel Lovers prefers the Air Viper 2025 as more playable, and Tom Pandore - Padel finds this year's racket much harder and more demanding than the 2024 version.

Reviewers rate it as a powerful, controllable option for intermediate and advanced players, and pdhsports picks it as the best racket in the Babolat Juan Lebrón range for a good amateur. Padel Review finds more ball output and easier depth than the regular Viper Juan Lebrón, but slightly less control and a woodier sound. Dani 13 says the player has to provide the speed and slow balls need pushing, and rates its hardness at 8 out of 10, so it is soft in name only.

Reviewers praise the control and handling, and Dani 13 and Probando Palas both liken it to the Nox AT10 12K, while Yannick Doston / Tenniszon recommends it to advanced players who want control and forgiveness. Opinions split on the net game: xTRES Padel does not quite like it at the volley and ranks it second to last in a Bullpadel line test, while Probando Palas finds volleys carry good weight at medium rhythm. Dani 13 and Tenniszon both say it is not for power players, and Dani 13 notes the ball can float on the bandeja if the downward gesture is short.

highlights.text: not quite like it at the volley

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the easy handling, control at the net and a slightly wider sweet spot. Power is where takes split: Mellis_YTB rates it 8.5 for power, below the Xplo at 9.5 and the Hack at 9, while Ariel Padel Reviews calls it strong on power for smashes. Reviewers also disagree on the rubber, as the4Set and Ariel Padel Reviews describe new hard EVA while Dani 13 and Hotel Palas say it ships with MultiEva, and Dani 13 does not find the change from last year worth an upgrade.

Reviewers praise the control and quick handling at the net, and two of them place it with upper-intermediate to advanced players rather than those still building technique. Practica Padel Team calls power standard with low ball exit at medium-low pace, while PadelCritic scores power at 8.9 for a low balance racket, so views on how much power it offers differ. Both place the standard Vertex 04 ahead on power, and xTRES Padel also finds less bandeja output than Paquito's racket or Delfi's.

highlights.text: control and quick handling at the net
low ball exit at medium-low pace

paras: Reviewers praise handling and control in a light diamond-shaped racket, and recommend it to attacking or all-round players at intermediate to advanced level. Power is where takes split: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi finds little power from the medium-low balance, while PadelCritic says it gives real pace on smashes and víboras. Padel Review finds it the stiffest Vertex Woman so far with a smaller sweet spot, while Padelful finds the sweet spot more generous than usual for a diamond.

Reviewers praise the smash power and say it suits intermediate-high players who attack and can make clean contact. Padel Review calls it the most powerful Bullpadel in the lineup but finds the spin disappointing, while Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel finds it more demanding than the 2026 version, with the higher balance slower in defence and volleys. Dani 13 finds it less forgiving than the Neuron, and Ariel Padel Reviews picks volleys as the best area despite a small sweet spot.

highlights.text: most powerful Bullpadel in the lineup

paras: Reviewers praise the smash power and the handling of this diamond shaped racket, and Simone Mazzola Padel and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi both see it suiting intermediate and advanced players. Padel Chiquito finds the Coello Pro better for attacking because of its higher balance, while Probando Palas prefers the Motion to the Siux Electra ST4 Pro on volleys but notes more loss of control at high pace. Reviewers describe the sweet spot as average or small, and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi calls the 350 euro price too high.

Reviewers praise how light and manoeuvrable it feels for a diamond shape, with net play and the bandeja as the main strengths, and it suits advanced or technical attacking players more than passive ones. Simone Mazzola Padel finds the power high and the handling easy, while Padelful and John Macallan / Padelmesh point to a small sweet spot and little help on slow defensive shots. Feel is also split: Padelful and John Macallan / Padelmesh call it medium-hard, but El chini consejo finds it softer than the Delta Motion and slightly less controllable than harder rackets.

Reviewers praise it at the net, with strong blocks, volleys and smashes, and recommend it to advanced players with a trained arm. Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel finds it more manageable and better for ball speed control than the Head Coello Pro, while the4Set finds the Coello Pro slightly more powerful but the Extreme Pro easier on defense. Spin is where takes split, as Padel Test by Roberto Cardi calls the 3D surface exceptional and the4Set lists the spin texture as an area to improve.

highlights.text: spin texture as an area to improve

paras: Reviewers praise the control, precision and placement of this 2026 teardrop, and recommend it to advanced players who build points rather than look for easy power. Probando Palas finds it more reactive and dynamic than the previous Radical Pro with a wide sweet spot, while PADELREVIEW ENG calls the touch as hard as the new Extreme Pro or harder and says it is not the fastest to maneuver. Padelful adds that the firmness can feel demanding over a long session, that mishits are exposed and that late contact drops the output.

Reviewers praise how easy it is to handle despite the 27 cm balance, along with a forgiving sweet spot and strong ball exit, and mostly place it with intermediate players. Takes split on spin: Padel Review and Fabio Ferro find the smooth faces give little grip, while Padel Test by Roberto Cardi and Practica Padel Team report cuts that bite well. Fabio Ferro finds the 2025 slightly stiffer than the 2023, which is still sold cheaper, and Padel Review questions paying 70 euros more for the newer version.

Reviewers praise the quick handling and dry, progressive response, and Padelful and PadelCritic place it with advanced or established intermediate players rather than beginners. Dani 13 calls the sweet spot wider than most rivals, while Probando Palas, Padelful and PadelCritic describe it as standard size, and Padelful, the only mixed take, adds that slow defensive balls get little help from the dry feel. Dani 13 finds it less bouncy than a Metalbone Hard but notes that fast volleys can send the ball to the glass, while Probando Palas prefers it to the Power Pro at high speeds.

Reviewers praise the comfort, handling and control of the 2025 model, and it suits players who want a controlled medium feel. Feel is where takes differ: Conect Padel finds it soft with a very wide sweet spot, while PADELARTE describes a hard, dry feel and only a medium sweet spot. Smash power is the most common limit, with Hotel Palas | La Suite del Padel and PadelCritic finding smashes less decisive than a diamond racket, though PADELARTE finds much more smash power than in the 2024 version.

highlights.text: less decisive than a diamond racket

paras: Reviewers praise the wide sweet spot and the mix of control and power, and Peter Consuegra and Practica Padel Team place it with intermediate players and above who want to defend and attack. Mixed takes mostly come from the comparison with the 18K: Conect Padel finds the 12K firmer, needing a longer swing and more arm push on lobs, and prefers the 18K for its softer feel. Probando Palas finds it works practically the same as the 2024 version, but notices the octagonal grip edges.

Reviewers praise the quick handling and comfort, with Dani 13 ranking it best in defence and Padelful finding it strongest at the net, so it suits players who value hand speed and control over raw power. Smashes divide opinion: PADELREVIEW ENG was surprised by the overhead power, while Dani 13 finds flat smashes lacking and Padelful misses authority. Dani 13 also notes the ball floats towards the glass at fast pace and that control is lower than on the AT10 18K with ML D rubber, and PADELREVIEW ENG calls the 340 euro price extremely high.

Reviewers praise it as easy to move, and it suits intermediate to advanced players who want a versatile racket that leans toward control. Fabio Ferro calls it the most powerful AT10 in recent years, but finds it stiffer, with less spin, a smaller sweet spot and a very high price at 389.90 euros, while Peter Consuegra finds more control than attack and less output than the Attack models. Dani 13 finds it forgiving in the volley zone but needs the tip pulled down to stop the ball floating on bandeja and vibora, and both Fabio Ferro and Dani 13 add weights to the head.

highlights.text: most powerful AT10 in recent years

paras: Reviewers suit it to attacking players who want good ball feel, praising the volley and aerial shots such as the bandeja, viper and rolled smash. Probando Palas finds that flat power smashes lack some progression and expects the AT10 12K Attack or EA10 Attack to do better there, while Padel Market calls the tip not very explosive. Peter Consuegra needed about two weeks to adjust to the higher balance and heavier head, which costs more to move in defence, though the racket still defends well.

highlights.text: flat power smashes lack some progression
costs more to move in defence

paras: Reviewers praise its control and handling, and place it with intermediate players who build points rather than rely on the smash. Padel Review is the mixed take, calling the 340 euro price high and finding it unstable at high pace with little smash power. Setup Padel | Mario Pazos loved it and calls it the most powerful racket in the control range, with a dry, firm feel unlike the softer classic ML10, while Padel Market sees it closer to a hybrid with a lot of ball feeling.

Reviewers praise the fast, manoeuvrable handling and the control at the net, and it suits intermediate to advanced players who hit actively. Probando Palas and Fabio Ferro both set it against the Babolat Air Viper, with Probando Palas finding it slightly more direct and controllable and Fabio Ferro noting a touch less ball exit. Sweet spot opinions differ, as PADELREVIEW ENG calls it tiny while Padel Test by Roberto Cardi finds it possibly slightly wider than the 2025, and John Macallan / Padelmesh adds that defence is the weakest area.

Reviewers describe it as a power racket, with Fabio Ferro calling it the most powerful Oxdog for upper intermediate and advanced players and rating its spin very good. Probando Palas finds its sweet spot more demanding than the Ultimate Pro and would pick the Ultimate Pro on the baseline. Dani 13 finds a slightly larger sweet spot than the Babolat Technical Viper 2025 but calls the weight of its 375 g sample a disadvantage for volleys.

Reviewers describe an offensive diamond for intermediate to advanced intermediate players, praised for a forgiving sweet spot, easy handling and controlled volleys. Opinions on movement differ: Probando Palas finds it moves well from the back, while PalaHack says it moves worse than lighter versions of the range. On power, Padel Test by Roberto Cardi places it below the Phenix Pro and Metalbone HRD, and Max Streltcoff / padel.how says flat smashes lack the heavy ball of the Ultimate Pro or Pro+.

Reviewers mostly praise stable, precise volleys and quick handling, and the racket suits intermediate to advanced players who build points rather than finish them. Feel is where takes split: Dani 13 measures lower hardness at about 4.5 out of 10 and says the ball sinks in at fast pace, while Padel Test by Roberto Cardi finds it firmer than earlier Diablo Pro models and Padelful calls it firm and lively. Forgiveness also varies, with Florian Döhnert-Breyer finding a generous sweet spot, but Padelful and Max Streltcoff / padel.how report limited help off centre.

highlights.text: ball sinks in at fast pace

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it for control, a wide sweet spot and net play, and recommend it to advanced and aggressive players. Handling is where takes split, as Dani 13 finds it very good while Padel Review finds it bulky to move and hard to use in defensive recoveries. Practica Padel Team and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi both find it softer than the Metalbone 3.4, whereas PadelCritic rates comfort and forgiveness at only 8.1 and notes vibration in long sessions.

Reviewers mostly place it with intermediate and advanced players and praise the spin from the sanded face, with several also noting easy handling. The sweet spot is where takes split: Dani 13 and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi find it wide, while Simone Mazzola Padel finds it unforgiving off centre and Fabio Ferro finds it lower than last year. Weight also divides opinion, as Padel Review's 375 g unit was hard to move and tired the arm, while Probando Palas and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi weighed 362 g and 363 g units and found them easy to handle.

highlights.text: 375 g unit was hard to move

paras: Reviewers praise the easy power and the grippy sandy finish, and Dani 13 and Setup Padel | Mario Pazos both point to backhand players as the target. Handling is where opinions split: Dani 13 finds the 369 g unit with a 27.1 cm balance hard to move in defence and volleys, while Setup Padel | Mario Pazos weighs a unit at 361 g with a balance of 27 and finds it moves well. Probando Palas finds it not the best from the back and a step below the Fenix Pro at full power, and Dani 13 finds control weaker than last year's Elite at medium and slow pace.

highlights.text: hard to move in defence and volleys
not the best from the back

paras: Reviewers praise the smash power and spin from the rough surface, and it suits advanced players who attack. Handling is where takes split: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi calls it very manoeuvrable and Simone Mazzola Padel finds it easy to move, while PadelCritic rates manoeuvrability as limited and the sweet spot as the smallest in its comparison. Dani 13 finds it more demanding than the Pro 4 when applying little force, and the stock grip wore out quickly for Padel Review and Simone Mazzola Padel.

Reviewers praise the power, especially on smashes and at the net, and point it at advanced attacking players, with Chingoland rating it probably the best value top signature racket. Opinions on the sweet spot split: Otro Nivel Padel finds it everywhere, while Padel Test by Roberto Cardi and Max Streltcoff / padel.how find it small and punishing off-centre. Probando Palas finds it demanding to move from the baseline, and Rens van Rijsewijk / Racketdoktor warns that vibration reaches the arm.

highlights.text: find it small and punishing off-centre
demanding to move from the baseline

paras: Reviewers praise the handling, the control and the smash on this 2026 racket, and it is described as suiting everyone from versatile intermediate players to advanced players who press points. Power is where takes differ: Probando Palas calls it not super powerful at high pace and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi misses a little top end power, while Tino finds power and control balanced and much more powerful than the Neuron. John Macallan / Padelmesh warns that the firm, dry feel can tire the arm in long matches and punishes passive defence, and Padel Test by Roberto Cardi thinks the 350 euro price is too high.

not super powerful at high pace
firm, dry feel can tire the arm

paras: Reviewers praise its net play and overheads, with Padel Review liking the explosive but controllable ball output and Peter Consuegra rating it strong on the víbora and smash. Feel is where opinions split: OngoalSweden finds it softer than StarVie rackets usually feel and more control than power, while Peter Consuegra finds it dry, hard and aimed at high level players. All three note a limited sweet spot, and OngoalSweden finds the Drax Plus gives more speed and forgives off-centre hits better, while Padel Review adds that the small, thin handle needs an overgrip.

highlights.text: strong on the víbora and smash

paras: Reviewers praise the big sweet spot, comfort and easy handling, and recommend it for intermediate players, with Padel Test by Roberto Cardi extending that up to pros. Power is where takes split: Padel Test by Roberto Cardi finds excellent power on the smash, vibora and bandeja, Padel FYI finds it better than expected, while Padel Review calls it not powerful and the flat smash weak. Against the Bela Pro, Padel FYI finds the LT about 15 g lighter and easier to move around, though the Pro is punchier.

Reviewers praise the spin and control, and most place it with intermediate players, with PADEL WORLD relaying players who preferred it to the heavier, harder Defy Pro. Sweet spot size is where opinions split: Extreme Padel finds it very small and unforgiving off-centre, while Probando Palas calls it well optimized and Padel Review calls it generous. Power also varies, as Fabio Ferro rates it high and Padel Review calls it only fair.

Reviewers mostly praise the long battery life and low price of this light OLED laptop, from almost 19 hours at 200 nits on the Ryzen 7 350 model (Just Josh) to about 10 hours on the Ryzen AI 7 350 with 32GB (Ryan's Tech Garage). Mixed takes come from speed, since the Ryzen AI 7 350 version has CPU results below last year's Ryzen 7 8840HS and the Intel version (Notebookcheck), while the older Ryzen 7 8840HS model performs almost identically and is the one to buy on sale (Just Josh). The 60Hz screen was a common criticism, with the Ryzen AI 7 350 unit's 1200p panel called dim at about 360 nits and a harder sell than the MacBook Air M4 at the expected $1,100 (Hardware Canucks).

Reviewers praise the ThinkPad keyboard and long battery life, with the Snapdragon X Elite version running roughly 20 hours or more in several light-use tests, and see it as an office laptop. Takes split by config: the Snapdragon model trails the MacBook Pro M3 in Cinebench (Andrew Marc David) and has app and driver gaps, the Ryzen AI 7 Pro 360 version kept its speed under sustained load where the Snapdragon throttled a bit (Notebookcheck), and the Core Ultra 5 228V version ran quieter and cooler but trails AMD and Snapdragon in multi-core (NotebookcheckReviews). The Ryzen 7 Zen 5 version ran extremely hot and loud under load at a $1,700 price that Just Josh called outrageous, and the 60Hz 1200p screen draws criticism from several reviewers.

highlights.text: extremely hot and loud under load

paras: Reviewers mostly recommend the base 16GB model for its speed, light fanless body and $999 starting price, with single-core scores about 21 percent above the M3 Air (Max Tech, Tom's Guide). Takes split on heat and upgrades: Snazzy Labs and Max Tech saw the fanless chassis throttle under sustained load, while 9to5Mac reported no throttling in eight months of everyday use, and Hardware Canucks and Tom's Guide point M1 Air users toward upgrading while M2 or M3 users wait. The 256GB base storage and two ports draw the most criticism (The Verge, 9to5Mac), and Created Tech found the Air a better default than the M4 MacBook Pro at $999 against $1599.

It suits gamers and creators who want a light, premium 14-inch machine and can live with fan noise and heat, with reviewers praising the OLED screen, speakers and aluminum build. Opinions split on value and comparisons: the 2023 G14 with RTX 4090 stays just ahead of the RTX 5080 version in most tests (Notebookcheck), the 2025 model is almost identical to the 2024 G14, which costs almost $2,000 less (Crimson Tech), and the Razer Blade 14 is nicer and quieter (PC Gamer). Several reviewers favor the RTX 5070 Ti version over the RTX 5080 version (Josh Craves Tech, PC Gamer, Matthew Moniz), and battery results vary from 10h 27min of web surfing at 150 nits on the RTX 5080 model (Notebookcheck) to 5-6 hours of general use on the RTX 5080 model (Tom's Guide).

highlights.text: OLED screen, speakers and aluminum build

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the body under 1 kg, the keyboard and the OLED, and on the Core Ultra 7 258V version with 32GB several measured longer battery life than the Gen 12 (Notebookcheck, Tom's Hardware). Mixed takes come from price and speed: PCWorld said it trails AMD chips and called the $2,519 price incredibly expensive, while Laptop Mag found multicore speed a letdown and noted the MacBook Pro 14 M4 lasted 18:32 against 11:28 here. Results on that same configuration still vary, from 16 hours 37 minutes in PCMark 10 (Andrew Marc David) to about 11 hours of web browsing, and Lunar Lake caps RAM at 32GB.

highlights.text: longer battery life than the Gen 12

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a desk-bound RTX 5090 laptop with strong performance, cool surfaces and an optional Cherry MX keyboard, and Trusted Reviews called it the most powerful gaming laptop they had tested. Mixed takes come from the screen and rivals: the MSI Raider 18 HX AI has a better mini-LED screen (PCMag UK), the Medion Erazer Beast 16 X1 Ultimate is nearly £1000 cheaper with better battery life (Trusted Reviews), and the HP Omen Max 16 came out marginally ahead in most gaming tests (PC Gamer). Battery was short on the RTX 5090 units, such as 1h 58min of web browsing in Notebookcheck's test, and PC Gamer found it cannot run at full power unplugged.

highlights.text: most powerful gaming laptop they had tested
cannot run at full power unplugged

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a quiet, fast everyday laptop, with the 16GB, 8-core GPU model beating the Dell XPS 13 in Geekbench (Laptop Mag) and lasting 14 hours 41 minutes on a web browsing test. Mixed takes come from heavy work, where Tech Radiator found the 8GB, 256GB model very hot and frustrating for video editing, and Max Tech saw about a 15% Cinebench drop on the 7-core GPU model once it heated up, though it still exported faster than the Intel Air (Max Tech). Against newer chips, everyday speed felt indistinguishable from the M3 or M4 (Created Tech), but the M1 scored 361 in Solar Bay Extreme against 2400 for the M4 Air (Luke Miani).

highlights.text: very hot and frustrating for video editing

paras: Reviewers mostly recommend it to students, commuters and moderate video editors who want a bigger screen in a light, quiet body, with Beebom measuring 13 to 14 hours on its M4 16GB unit and Tom's Guide 15 hours 14 minutes in a web test on its 16GB and 256GB unit. Opinions split on sustained load: Kevin Ferrandiz found the top and keyboard uncomfortably hot in a programming benchmark, though less than on the 13-inch M4 (Kevin Ferrandiz), while The Verge saw throttling in Photoshop and Lightroom Classic and Macwelt measured the M4 MacBook Pro six percent ahead in a stress test thanks to active cooling (Macwelt). Some reviewers see little reason to upgrade from the M3 (Beebom, Tom's Guide, Macwelt), and Tom's Guide calls the 13-inch M4 Air the pick for most people, with this as second choice (Tom's Guide).

highlights.text: throttling in Photoshop and Lightroom Classic

paras: Reviewers praise the 15-inch M5 Air as a silent, fast machine with a roomy screen and long battery life, suited to browser-heavy work, multitasking and light creative jobs. Mixed takes come mostly from price and the cheaper MacBook Neo: casual buyers are pointed to the Neo (The Verge, 6 Months Later, Noah Herman), M4 Air buyers are told to expect modest gains (Tom's Guide) or to skip it (The Verge), and heavy creative work still suits a MacBook Pro (Noah Herman). Battery results vary by test, from 13 to 14 hours of mixed use on the 16GB model with 1TB (The Verge) to 17 hours 12 minutes of browsing at 150 nits on the 32GB, 2TB unit (Notebookcheck), while Adam Talks Tech notes the fanless body throttles 15 to 20% under long heavy loads.

Reviewers mostly praise it as a fast, quiet laptop with a bright display, and Intel Mac users are the clearest upgraders (Ryan Gehret, HardwareZone Singapore). The main split is chip choice: the M4 Pro CPU beat the M3 Max (MobileTechReview), the M4 Pro matched the M4 Max in single core but trailed it in graphics and export (Max Tech), and the 14-inch M4 Max landed within 1% of the 16-inch (Matt Talks Tech), yet SoulOfTech called the Max unnecessary for most buyers. Steep upgrade pricing draws criticism (Notebookcheck, HardwareZone Singapore), and Alex Blogoodf, using an M4 Pro, got migraines from PWM flicker, while Notebookcheck called the PWM rate on its M4 Pro high enough for most users.

highlights.text: fast, quiet laptop with a bright display
Intel Mac users are the clearest upgraders

paras: Reviewers who tested the base M4 with 16GB praise its fast everyday performance, long battery life, speakers and keyboard, and often suggest it for people stepping up from a MacBook Air (The Verge, TechRadar). Opinion splits on the $150 nano-texture screen: it cut glare clearly against a glossy MacBook Pro 16-inch M4 Pro (Laptop Mag), while Just Josh, on an M4 Pro 12-core model, noticed grain and a screen door effect, and Macworld found less vibrant colors. The base model's single fan is the other sore point, with Notebookcheck measuring 45.9 dB(A) under sustained load, louder than the M4 Pro at 44.5 dB(A) (Notebookcheck).

highlights.text: grain and a screen door effect

paras: Reviewers praise the base M5 14-inch for its bright screen, long battery life and much faster SSD, and it suits video editors and developers who do not need a Pro chip, as well as upgraders from older Macs. Value is where takes split: the MacBook Air M4 is cheaper and close in performance for light work (André Creates, Brandon Butch), the M4 Pro is faster for heavy 3D, music and code work (SPACE DESIGN WAREHOUSE), and the M5 is a less compelling step for M4 users (The Verge, PCMag Australia). The single fan is a recurring complaint, with Max Tech measuring chip temps near 100°C in a 10 minute Cinebench run on the 16GB model and Notebookcheck logging 48 dB(A) under full load on the 32GB unit.

highlights.text: single fan is a recurring complaint
less compelling step for M4 users

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it for video and other creative work, with the display, speakers and ports liked on both the M4 Pro and M4 Max versions. Upgrade advice depends on what is being replaced: the M4 Max gives little reason to leave an M3 Max (The Tech Chap), while the base M4 Pro cut a 4K render from about 5 minutes to about 4 minutes against an M1 Pro (Dave on Tech). Noise and heat reports differ: the M4 Pro 16-inch stayed far quieter than a 14-inch M4 Pro in a Cinebench stress test (Mark's Tech), while the M4 Max ran hotter and louder in high performance mode (The Tech Chap), though some other M4 Max reviewers found the fans quiet.

highlights.text: little reason to leave an M3 Max

paras: Reviewers praise the speed and efficiency for heavy video, development and local AI work, with the M5 Max about 8% ahead of the M4 Max in multi-core (Hardware Canucks) and 12 percent ahead (Macworld). Takes split on whether the Max is needed: the 18-core M5 Pro is the developer sweet spot (Alex Ziskind), while the Max suits those who want 128GB for very large models (ZXTech), and M4 Max users can skip it unless disk-heavy work matters (Macworld). Noise and heat vary, with coil whine on M5 Max units (Hardware Canucks, ZXTech) and a chassis too hot for the lap (ZXTech), yet Just Josh found the fans quiet on the Pro and Max they tested.

highlights.text: coil whine on M5 Max units
a chassis too hot for the lap

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it as a fast, light creator convertible with an accurate OLED and a keyboard with 1.7 mm travel, though many flag the 60Hz panel and loud fans under load. Battery is where takes split: the RTX 4050 version managed about 8 hours of light use, roughly 5 hours less than a Snapdragon Surface Laptop (MobileTechReview), the RTX 4050 model reached 9:28 of web surfing at 150 nits, well behind the MacBook Air M3 and Surface Pro 11 (Tom's Guide), and the RTX 4070 version drew 60 to 80 W against about 20 W for a MacBook Pro M4 Pro (Tech Notice). Drawing is also mixed: Brad Colbow, on the RTX 4060 version, found the stylus and palm rejection weak, while Teoh on Tech, on the RTX 4050 version, found pen drawing better than on a Surface Pro (Teoh on Tech) but saw wobble on slow diagonal lines.

Reviewers praise the integrated graphics in a sturdy 13.4-inch tablet, with the Radeon 8060S rated near an RTX 4060 laptop (The Verge) and level with an RTX 4070 Laptop (Notebookcheck). Mixed takes come from price and battery: a Zephyrus G14 with an RTX 5070 costs the same or less and performs better (Engadget), a ROG Ally plus a MacBook Air costs less (ryanOC), and the Max+ 395 and 32GB model manages about an hour of demanding games on battery (UFD Tech, Retro Game Corps). Battery for lighter work varies by mode, from about 7 hours in eco mode (MobileTechReview) to 10 hours in a rundown (The Verge) on the tested 32GB units.

highlights.text: about an hour of demanding games

paras: Reviewers praise it as a fast, cool-running gaming laptop with easy RAM and SSD access, suited to gamers who want a desktop replacement more than a portable. The Ryzen 9 9955HX3D and RTX 5070 Ti unit was called a worthy, slightly cheaper rival to the Lenovo Legion Pro 7i Gen 10 (PCWorld), the Core Ultra 9 275HX and RTX 5070 Ti model scored lower in Cinebench R23 than a Legion Pro 7 or Asus G18 (Binosha Tech), and a $1700 Legion with an OLED screen was pointed to as an alternative after the price was called too high (Jarrod'sTech). Digit's take was mixed, over the price and 8GB of VRAM on the RTX 5070 model, and battery results vary by use on Core Ultra 9 275HX models, from about 1 hour 20 minutes of intense gaming (Digit) to about one full day of browsing and movies (Roberto Jorge Tech).

Reviewers who tested the RTX 5080 version mostly praise it as a fast desk machine with a tool-free bottom panel, and say it is too heavy at about 3.2 kg to travel with. Opinions split on how it stacks up: it outscored the HP Omen Max 16 with an RTX 5090 in benchmarks (Laptop Mag), while it ran about 5% fewer frames than other 5080 laptops such as the HP Omen 16 (Dan's Tech House), and the Strix G16 is called lighter with almost the same performance (Binosha Tech). Battery results also vary, from 4 hours 34 minutes of YouTube playback (Crimson Tech) to 7 hours 45 minutes in a non-gaming test (Laptop Mag), and CPU heat of 103°C (Crimson Tech) and a loud Turbo mode (THE ROCO) were the main complaints.

Reviewers who tested it praise it for people who want desktop-level gaming power, with a very bright mini-LED screen and a base panel that opens without tools for RAM and SSD upgrades. Mixed takes come from value: the RTX 5080 version matched the cheaper Strix G18 in Cinebench and Time Spy (Crimson Tech), the RTX 5070 Ti version was picked over the RTX 5080 for $800 less (Tom's Honest Tips), and the smaller Scar 16 was pointed to for similar performance in a lighter body (Jarrod'sTech). Battery life is short, from about two hours unplugged on the RTX 5080 loaner (MobileTechReview) to 5 h 32 min of WLAN use on the RTX 5090 model (Notebookcheck), which also saw only a small lead over the old RTX 4090 Laptop at native resolution (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers who tested the RTX 5070 Ti Intel versions praise the brighter OLED, keyboard and speakers, and see high-end gaming in a 14-inch body for people who can afford it. Price drives most of the mixed takes, with last year's AMD G14 called the more sensible buy (The Verge), the $2599 2025 model suggested for buyers skipping HDR gaming (Notebookcheck), and last year's model preferred over the $3,600 start (Crimson Tech), though Jarrod'sTech says the new model is worth the extra if budget allows. Battery results depend on the test, from over 15 hours of light use (Crimson Tech) and over 17 hours in a rundown (The Verge) to 8:32 of web surfing (Tom's Guide), and a cheaper M5 MacBook Pro 14 beats it or comes close in CPU tasks (The Verge).

Reviewers praise the OLED screen, speakers and aluminum build in a thin, light body, and it suits buyers who want portability more than top gaming speed. Mixed takes mostly come from power limits: the 120 W RTX 5080 model lags higher-wattage rivals, and a similarly priced Razer Blade 16 is preferred (PC Gamer), while Just Josh advises the RTX 5070 Ti over the 5080 and 5090 configs and Josh Craves Tech expects 5070 Ti buyers to be happiest. Battery and noise depend on the config and mode, with Just Josh recording over 10 hours of light use on the RTX 5080 version, Crimson Tech getting a little over 6 hours of YouTube playback on the RTX 5070 Ti model, and several reviewers calling turbo mode loud.

highlights.text: OLED screen, speakers and aluminum build

paras: Reviewers mostly praise a light 14-inch body, cool running and long battery life in light use, with almost 9 to 10 hours in power saving mode on the Ryzen 7 / RTX 5050 model (IRob.) and 9 hours 46 minutes in silent mode on the Ryzen AI 7 350 / RTX 5060 unit (Duy Luân Dễ Thương). Mixed takes come from the CPU and price: the Ryzen AI 7 350 is a small step down from last year's Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 model, and the $1,699 price, up $200, is hard to justify (Tom's Guide), while last year's Ryzen 9 model for about $300 less is called the smarter buy (Grobal Tech). Gaming on battery is short, at 1:45 on the RTX 5060 / 16GB model (Tom's Guide) and 1 hour 21 minutes on the RTX 5060 / 32GB model (Dream Seed).

Reviewers mostly recommend it to budget-minded gamers, praising strong frame rates and cooling, with Binosha Tech calling cooling excellent on the Ryzen 7 260 version and citytel finding temperatures among the best they had seen on the RTX 5070 model. Mixed takes come from noise and price: Notebookcheck found Turbo mode very loud at 57.1 dB(A) on its RTX 5070 unit, TechRadar called the fans a cacophony on the RTX 5050 unit, and the XMG Core 16 with the same RTX 5070 is about 300 euros cheaper (Notebookcheck), while the Acer Nitro 16 AMD is a cheaper option (TechRadar). Crimson Tech found the RTX 5070 model not much faster than the RTX 5060 one, so called the 5060 the better value.

Reviewers mostly praise it for portable everyday use, with long battery life, a light metal body and a good port selection. Battery results depend on the config: the Core Ultra 5 226V/16GB model ran 22h 10min of local video playback (Jagat Review) and 17h 10min in a Wi-Fi test (Notebookcheck), while the Core Ultra 7 258V/32GB model reached 13h 35min in a Premiere Pro loop (TheHikaku) and about 14 hours (Binosha Tech). Opinions split on price and screen: the AMD version runs hotter and louder than this Intel model (Notebookcheck), the older Core Ultra 7 155H Vivobook S 14 is the cheaper pick on a tight budget (Nerd Reviews ID), and the OLED panel trails the MacBook Air and Yoga Slim 7i screens (Binosha Tech), while several reviewers found the 60Hz panel glossy and reflective.

Reviewers mostly praise the weight of about 1 kg or less and battery life that lasts a full day or more on the Snapdragon X and X Plus models, and see it fitting students, travelers and office users rather than gamers or heavy video editors. Mixed takes come from price and build: Just Josh calls $1,100 overpriced and the body cheap feeling, PCWorld calls the entry chip a $600 laptop part in a $1,200 machine, while Max Tech calls it one of the best value laptops at $900 to $1,100. On comparisons, it is lighter than a MacBook Air by about 300 g (Jon Valiagas) and outlasted a MacBook Air 13 with M3 in a streaming test (The Tech Chap), though the MacBook Air M3 needs 11 watts for a similar Cinebench score against 25 watts for the Snapdragon X model (Just Josh).

highlights.text: weight of about 1 kg or less
battery life that lasts a full day or more

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the two OLED screens and detachable keyboard as a useful built-in second display for multitasking and editing on the Core Ultra 9 version. Battery with both screens on is the main split, from 5 to 5.5 hours (Hassan Govani) to a little over 8 hours on the Full HD panel model (NotebookcheckReviews), and PCWorld called it heavy and pricey. On comparisons, one reviewer found the Yoga Book 9i thinner and more premium but costlier (TechniQualities), and another found it better than a Surface Pro 11 for multitasking but less efficient (Spencer Ryan).

Reviewers mostly praise the long battery life, quiet fans and 120Hz OLED in a body of about 2.65 lb, with the Core Ultra 7 258V version reaching 21 hours of video in PCWorld's test and nearly 19 hours in Just Josh's. Mixed takes come from price and rivals: the Lenovo Slim 7i Aura Edition is the better buy for most people (Just Josh), the Ryzen-based Zenbook S 16 is faster at the same price (UFD Tech), and the Vivobook S14 with Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 has more than twice the multicore performance for $200 to $300 less (Hubwood). Multi-core speed is the common complaint, with the 258V model settling near 17 watts and losing around 30 percent of multi-core performance under constant load (Notebookcheck).

highlights.text: Multi-core speed is the common complaint

paras: Reviewers praise the light aluminium body, and Notebookcheck measured 18.5 hours of WiFi web surfing on the Core Ultra 7 268V unit with the 68 Wh battery, which costs extra. Reviewers agree on CPU speed: Notebookcheck calls CPU speed modest and far behind the EliteBook X G1a 14 in Cinebench (Notebookcheck), while パソコンガイド and Pasokon Guide rate multi-core speed as low but find the graphics good enough for light editing. Heat is the other catch on the Core Ultra 7 units, with パソコンガイド recording 50.4°C at the surface under full load and Pasokon Guide noting 47.2 degrees on the bottom, which they call hot on the lap.

Reviewers praise the 15-inch Legion 5 Gen 10 as a light gaming laptop with a bright 165Hz OLED screen and a good keyboard, suited to gamers who also edit. Battery life is where takes split: the Ryzen 7 260 and RTX 5060 version reached more than 9 and a half hours of Wi-Fi use (NotebookcheckReviews), while the Core Ultra 7 and RTX 5070 version managed a little over 3 hours (ThinkView). On GPU choice, Tech Guy Beau advises the Ryzen 7 260 with an RTX 5050 or 5060 over the RTX 5070, GamesRadar+ names the RTX 5070 as the sweet spot, and Notebookcheck (DE) found the RTX 5060 only 7% behind the 115 W RTX 5070 in the Razer Blade 14 2025.

Reviewers praise the 15.1-inch OLED panel, the keyboard and the performance for about $1,200 to $1,400, and it suits buyers who want a compact OLED gaming laptop. Comparisons mostly favor it: the RTX 5060 UK model scored ahead of the Asus TUF Gaming A14 in Time Spy (Tom's Guide), it beats a ThinkPad P14s on performance but loses on battery life (Slap Tech), and the Gigabyte Aero X16 is lighter to carry but has a weaker GPU and display (Just Josh). Takes split on noise and battery: the Arrow Lake HX RTX 5060 model had the quietest fans in its group and about 8 hours with the dedicated GPU disabled (Just Josh), while the RTX 5070 model lasted a little over 3 hours (ThinkView) and the Core i7-13650HX UK model's fans were about twice as loud as the TUF Gaming A14's in Cyberpunk (Tom's Guide).

Reviewers mostly praise it as a plugged-in gaming machine, with RTX 5080 performance, a bright 240 Hz OLED at around 500 nits and a good keyboard singled out. Opinions differ on how far ahead it is: one reviewer rated the RTX 5080 version the most performant RTX 5080 laptop tested but would still pick the Razer Blade 16 as a personal go-to (PC Gamer), while default mode trailed the Asus ROG Strix Scar 16 and Gigabyte Aorus Master 16 until performance mode was turned on (Tom's Hardware), and the RTX 5090 pre-production unit gained at most 20% over the 2024 RTX 4090 model (Hardware Canucks). Battery life is the common complaint, about 4.5 to 5.5 hours of light use on the RTX 5080 version, along with the heavy 400 W charger, side-mounted ports and loud fans in performance mode.

highlights.text: Battery life is the common complaint

paras: Reviewers who tested the RTX 5060 version mostly see a solid 1080p gaming laptop with a strong keyboard and easy RAM and SSD upgrades. Alternatives differ by reviewer: the Legion 5 is suggested for roughly 200 more in Germany (NotebookcheckReviews), the Asus TUF A16 is preferred at the same price (Crimson Tech), and the Gigabyte Aero 16 with an RTX 5060 is pointed to for $150 less (Matthew Moniz). Battery results depend on the config, with well over 6 hours on the RTX 5060 version (Matthew Moniz), 4.5 hours of Wi-Fi browsing on another RTX 5060 unit (Notebookcheck) and about 2 hours of mixed use on the RTX 5050 model (The Silicon Foxx).

Reviewers mostly praise the keyboard, the aluminum lid and the room to upgrade RAM and SSDs, and point it at office work and students rather than gaming. Mixed takes come from the configuration: the Ryzen 7 250 model was clearly ahead of the E14 Gen 6 but behind the Core Ultra 7 255H version (Notebookcheck), which that site calls the better buy, while TuttoTech found its 32GB Core Ultra 7 258V config costly because it pairs with the basic 60Hz screen, and the 2.8K 120Hz panel adds only 10 euro. Single-channel memory held back graphics on the 8GB Core Ultra 5 225H unit (Hendrik Widarmawan) and on the 16GB single-stick Core Ultra 5 225H unit (TheHikaku), so a second module matters.

highlights.text: room to upgrade RAM and SSDs

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the keyboard, the bright tandem OLED and the light 16-inch build, and StorageReview calls it the pick for engineers and creatives who travel. Battery results on Core Ultra 7 OLED models range widely, from 16 hours of video playback (PCMag UK) to 5 hours 28 minutes of Wi-Fi browsing (Notebookcheck), and AICvideo got 4 to 5 hours at default settings. On speed, the 16-inch MacBook Pro with M4 Max is faster and more efficient in benchmarks (Andrew Marc David), while AICvideo measured performance only 10 to 12% above the ThinkPad P1 Gen 7 and Notebookcheck measured CPU multi-thread speed 15 to 20 percent above it.

highlights.text: pick for engineers and creatives who travel

paras: Reviewers mostly like it as a business typing machine, with PCMag Australia calling the keyboard the gold standard and Rodrigo Vieira - RSSV calling it the best for long typing in months. Battery life depends on the config: the Core Ultra 7 258V model lasted 19h 22min in a web surfing test (Notebookcheck) and the Core Ultra 5 225U model managed 19 hours 9 minutes of video playback (PCMag Australia), while Tech Guy Beau estimated eight or nine hours in light use on the AMD 350 model. Takes are mixed on screens and rivals, as LongRhino rated the Full HD 60Hz screen basic on the Core Ultra 7 255U model, and the ThinkPad T14s felt denser and had a better webcam than the AMD 350 T14 (Tech Guy Beau).

Reviewers praise this ThinkPad convertible for its keyboard, metal build and long battery life on the Core Ultra 7 258V models, and it suits office and business buyers more than power users. Battery results depend on the panel: Notebookcheck logged 21h 58min of web browsing on the IPS model, Trusted Reviews logged 14 hours 13 minutes in PCMark 10 on the OLED model with the Dell Pro 14 Premium lasting several hours longer (Trusted Reviews), and Riccardo Palombo puts the IPS 60Hz panel at about 3 hours more than OLED. Heat and clocks draw the mixed takes, with the CPU reaching 96°C and cutting frequency (Riccardo Palombo) and Slap Tech advising against modern PC gaming after power dropped to 8 watts.

highlights.text: keyboard, metal build and long battery life

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the long battery life, cool and quiet running and the keyboard, though runtimes depend on the unit: the Core Ultra 7 256V 16GB model lasted 14:10 in Tom's Guide's battery test and 16 hours 45 minutes in PCWorld's video loop, while the 14-inch OLED Core 7 model managed 7 to 8 hours (The Wolf of Williamsburg). Complaints centre on multi-core speed, where the Yoga Slim 7x offers stronger performance for similar money (Laptop Mag), and on the IPS panel instead of OLED, which Tom's Guide and PCWorld both marked down. Mash IT chose the 32GB Core Ultra 7 258V Yoga over the 15-inch MacBook Air M3 for costing £300 less, though the Air lasted longer in their streaming test (Mash IT).

Reviewers praise it as a full Windows tablet for office work and travel, with battery life around 12 hours in several tests, including the Snapdragon X Elite OLED model (Tom's Guide) and the X Plus LCD model (ETA PRIME). Opinions split on value and the alternatives: Max Tech would buy it over the M4 iPad Pro for full Windows apps (Max Tech), Tom's Guide points to that iPad as a cheaper option for people who dislike Windows, and UFD Tech says a MacBook Air can match its battery life and performance in many cases (UFD Tech). Price and Arm support draw the criticism, with one reviewer setting the base model with keyboard at about $2,000 against about $1,500 for an M3 MacBook Air (Spixel), and The Verge advising a wait of about six months to see how Arm compatibility settles.

highlights.text: Price and Arm support draw the criticism

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 versions for gaming performance per dollar, with two Thunderbolt 5 ports and a sturdy build, and it suits plugged-in use better than carrying around. Mixed takes come from noise and the screen: the top performance or extreme modes are very loud, balanced mode loses little frame rate (Mash IT, Hubwood), and three reviewers advise skipping the 1080p panel option (Jarrod'sTech, GizmoSlipTech, Tech Guy Beau). Against other laptops, the 5070 Ti version's Time Spy score sits 5% behind a 175W RTX 4080 laptop (Mash IT), the Alienware 16 Area-51's RTX 5080 is around 20% faster (Notebookcheck), and the Schenker XMG Pro 16 lasts about nine hours in a Wi-Fi test against about 7 hours for the Core Ultra 7 5070 Ti Vector (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers mostly praise the aluminum build, the 120Hz OLED and the gaming performance in a body of about 3.5 to 3.6 lb, and it suits buyers who want portability over raw power. Mixed takes come from price and GPU headroom: Jarrod'sTech would buy the Zephyrus G14 with an RTX 5070 Ti at the same price, while Notebookcheck found that version about 14% faster in synthetic GPU tests but about 1000 Euros more, with a small gap at 1080p. Battery results differ by test and config, with PCMag UK recording 11:37 of video playback on the RTX 5070 model and TechRadar 5 hours 1 minute of web surfing in Performance mode on the same GPU.

Reviewers mostly like it for office, browsing and light editing, praising the thin fanless body, MagSafe, the 1080p webcam and the speakers. Mixed takes come from sustained load and price: the fanless chassis throttles in long renders (Marques Brownlee), though Snazzy Labs calls the throttling mild, and the M1 Air is the cheaper pick for most buyers (CNET, Tom's Hardware), while professionals are pointed to the 14-inch MacBook Pro (Jon Valiagas, Arthur Winer). The base 256GB model draws the sharpest criticism, since its single NAND chip makes the SSD slower, with Macworld measuring read speeds 47.9 percent below the 1TB model and recommending the upgraded configuration or an M1 Air (Macworld).

Reviewers praise the 13-inch M3 Air as a light, silent, fanless laptop with long battery life, suited to students, travelers and light creative users, with several recommending the 16GB version for editing. Battery figures depend on use: web surfing ran about 15 hours on the 8GB base model (Tom's Guide) and on the 16GB, 10-core GPU model (Notebookcheck), while the 16GB version dropped to 4 to 5 hours of video editing (Leo Does Tech). On the upgrade question, it beats the M2 Air in benchmarks (Tom's Guide), yet an M2 Air is described as nearly as capable and cheaper (Byte Review), and the M3 MacBook Pro is preferred for heavy editing because of its extra ports and ProMotion display (6 Months Later).

Reviewers praise the fanless 15-inch Air as a big, quiet everyday laptop, with Notebookcheck measuring 16 hours 56 minutes of web surfing on the 16GB, 512GB model and Tom's Guide 15 hours 3 minutes on its 16GB, 512GB unit. Mixed takes come mostly from memory and cooling: the 8GB model stuttered under heavy multitasking for Zanzebek, while Melih Gungor - MTG saw no lag in Final Cut Pro on 8GB, and the MacBook Pro 14 finished a 4K transcode nearly a minute faster (Tom's Guide) while costing only about $100 more at matched specs (Matthew Moniz). Some reviewers point buyers who skip heavy work to the cheaper MacBook Air 15 M2 (Wylsacom) and advise M2 users not to upgrade (Notebookcheck).

Reviewers see it suiting buyers who want the Touch Bar, a fan and very long battery life, with a clear speed gain over the M1 in benchmarks such as Cinebench (ShortCircuit). Most still point to other laptops: the MacBook Air M2 as the better deal (Tom's Guide, The Verge) and the 14-inch MacBook Pro for serious work (Engadget, Karl Conrad). Config matters, since the base 256GB SSD is slower than the M1 version (Max Tech) and the 8GB model ran out of memory in a game and Premiere Pro (Matthew Moniz), while 18 hours 20 minutes of web surfing came from the 16GB and 1TB unit (Tom's Guide).

highlights.text: clear speed gain over the M1
256GB SSD is slower than the M1

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it for video editing and daily work, with the mini-LED screen, speakers and returning ports as regular highlights. Mixed takes start with the M1 Max GPU, which landed closer to an RTX 3050 Ti than an RTX 3080 outside video work (Linus Tech Tips) and lost Redshift to an ASUS Zephyrus M16 (Linus Tech Tips), while the 10-core M1 Pro was rated ahead of the Dell XPS 13 and Razer Blade 14 on performance, display and battery life, though both cost less (Tom's Guide). Noise and battery depend on the config, with a fair amount of fan noise in intense benchmarks on the 10-core 32GB M1 Pro (PCMag UK) against near silence and about 6 hours of battery under heavy load on an M1 Pro (Arthur Winer).

highlights.text: mini-LED screen, speakers and returning ports
a fair amount of fan noise

paras: Reviewers praise the CPU speed, sturdy build, speakers and mini LED screen, with battery runs of 17 hours 58 minutes on the M5 Max with 128GB (Tom's Hardware) and 9 hours 18 minutes on the M5 Pro with 24GB (ShortCircuit). Heat is where takes split: the 14-inch M5 Max with 64GB went past 100°C in full benchmarks and scored slightly below the 16-inch M5 Max (Mark's Tech), while the 128GB M5 Max saw performance drop 24% in a stress test (Notebookcheck). Some also question the Max, since the extra $900 over the Pro buys little in video editing (Luke Miani) and the M5 Pro 15 core is the pick for most buyers (Just Josh).

highlights.text: sturdy build, speakers and mini LED screen
performance drop 24% in a stress test

paras: Reviewers mostly praise it for video and photo editing, the mini LED screen and the speakers, and several found the M1 Pro model already fast enough, while Tom's Guide found the 14-inch M1 Pro nearly as fast as the M1 Max (Tom's Guide). Mixed takes come from the M1 Max: Dayo Aworunse reproduced a MagSafe charging fault with the 140W adapter on a shut down 16-inch, and The Everyday Dad hit slow monitor and drive detection on Monterey, suggesting an M1 Mac mini may end up as fast for docked work (The Everyday Dad). Lee's Tech Down Under, using the M1 Pro, advises against upgrading from an M1 MacBook Air without spare cash (Lee's Tech Down Under).

Reviewers mostly praise the mini-LED screen, video export speed and battery life, and say it suits creative pros and people coming from Intel or older machines. Most tell M1 Pro and M1 Max users to skip it, with the M2 Max about 20 percent faster in multi-core than the M1 Max (The Verge) and the M2 Pro about 20 percent ahead of the M1 Pro in most tests (Macworld), though the base M2 Pro ran hotter than the 2021 M1 Pro (Max Tech). Battery results depend on the config, from about 12 hours of mixed use on an M2 Max with 64GB (Terafied) to 18 hours 56 minutes of web surfing on a maxed-out M2 Max (Tom's Guide), and refurbished 2021 models are suggested over it on price (The Tech Chap).

Reviewers mostly praise it as a light creator laptop with fast editing, an accurate OLED screen, a good keyboard and a touchpad dial, suited to video and photo editors who can live without a higher refresh rate. Takes split on noise and heat: Notebookcheck measured fans up to 53.2 dB(A) on the RTX 4070 and 64GB model, while Ben G Kaiser measured 35 to 40 dB in whisper mode on a 32GB unit, at the cost of a 4 minutes 42 seconds export against 2 minutes 29 seconds plugged in. On GPU power and battery, the ROG Zephyrus G16 2024 has a much faster RTX 4080 (Notebookcheck), and Andres Vidoza found the 16-inch MacBook Pro M3 Max better for battery and sustained power unplugged (Andres Vidoza), though the tested config costs almost $2,000 Canadian less.

Reviewers praise the bright mini-LED screen, the keyboard and tool-free RAM and SSD access, and most see it as a desktop replacement because the chassis is heavy and the charger is large. Alternatives raised include the Lenovo Legion Pro 7i for its OLED display (PCWorld), the HP Omen Max 16 as a serious contender (Matthew Moniz), and the ROG Zephyrus G14 for carrying around (Jon Valiagas). Battery results vary widely, for example 8 hours 23 minutes of local video playback (PCMag Middle East) against about 2.5 hours in iGPU mode (TechHook), both on the RTX 5080 version.

highlights.text: heavy and the charger is large

paras: It suits gamers who want a big screen and desktop-class power, and reviewers such as MobileTechReview and PC Gamer single out the bright mini-LED panel as the high point. Comparisons are mixed: the RTX 4090 version trails the MSI Titan 18 HX by 7 to 10% in games but costs far less (GizmoSlipTech), it reaches more than 7 and a half hours in a Wi-Fi test against little over 4 hours for the Titan (Notebookcheck), and last year's Scar 18 is the better buy unless the brighter screen matters (Jarrod'sTech). Battery life varies a lot by test, with about 3.5 hours at 200 nits on the RTX 4080 model (MobileTechReview), and criticism centres on the plastic build and a high price for modest gains.

Reviewers who liked it point to the 4K mini-LED screen, cooling that holds full power in the RTX 5090 models, and the toolless bottom panel, and see it as a desktop replacement for buyers with a deep budget. Mixed takes come from price and rivals: last year's SCAR 18 gives about 95% of the experience for buyers who skip ELMB, at a lower price (Matthew Moniz), the Lenovo Legion 9i is the better 18-inch pick because it costs less (Jarrod'sTech), and it trailed the Razer Blade 18 by close to 10% at 4K in several games (Tom's Hardware). Battery on RTX 5090 versions ran from about four hours (Notebookcheck) to just under six in a video loop (PCMag UK), and the weight is high enough that reviewers keep it on a desk.

Reviewers mostly praise the OLED screen, aluminum build and speakers, and see it suiting buyers who want a light 14-inch laptop for gaming and creative work. Opinions split on speed and battery: the 90W RTX 4070 version performs like an RTX 4060 laptop (Tom's Hardware) and sits just behind the Razer Blade 14 in Cyberpunk 2077 (Engadget), while battery varies, with 6 hours 45 minutes on the RTX 4070 model (Tom's Hardware) and nearly 10 hours on the RTX 4070 32GB model (ShortCircuit). It is rated ahead of the MacBook Pro 14 for gaming, keyboard, speakers and value, though behind it for HDR work and runtimes (Notebookcheck), and several reviewers flag soldered RAM, which Notebookcheck calls the main weakness.

highlights.text: OLED screen, aluminum build and speakers

paras: Reviewers praise the thin aluminium body, the 240Hz OLED screen and the speakers, and it suits buyers who want a light 16-inch machine more than top frame rates. Fan noise splits opinions: Just Josh found that none of the units tested were quiet, including the RTX 4070 version, while TechOdyssey found the fans not too loud on the Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 and RTX 4070 model. Lenovo's Legion 7i is seen as the main rival because its memory is upgradeable (Jarrod'sTech), and Hardware Canucks advises the Ryzen AI 9 version over the Intel one.

highlights.text: none of the units tested were quiet

paras: Reviewers praise the bright OLED and speakers and the much longer battery life on RTX 5080 versions, so it suits buyers who put portability first and can afford it. Value is where takes split: the Razer Blade 16 is faster (Notebookcheck and NotebookcheckReviews) and costs $400 less in RTX 5080 trim (PC Gamer), while last year's G16 is suggested as the cheaper route (Jarrod'sTech and Matthew Moniz). Turbo mode is loud, and Manual mode at 160W runs hotter for little gain over Turbo (Dan's Tech House and PC Gamer).

Reviewers who tested the Ryzen 9 versions praised the CPU power, gaming frame rates and 165Hz screen for the price, and the RTX 4060 model with the Ryzen 9 7845HX came out ahead of the ROG Zephyrus G16 in a 4K render, 11 minutes against about 14 (Roberto Jorge Tech), and was picked over the TUF F15 for budget gaming (Haviq Tech). Takes were mixed on the Ryzen 7 7445HS and RTX 4050 model, which had the weakest CPU of the three and lost on value to the Lenovo LOQ (Geeky Piyush). Battery life varied, at 2 to 4 hours on the RTX 4070 version (GizmoSlipTech) and 2 to 3 hours on the RTX 4060 version (Hashan De Zoysa), against a 6 to 7 hour YouTube estimate on the Ryzen 9 7845HX model (Roberto Jorge Tech).

highlights.text: ahead of the ROG Zephyrus G16

paras: Reviewers mostly suit it to work and travel, praising the light aluminum body, the 120Hz OLED touchscreen and the keyboard, with 14 hours 18 minutes in a modern office battery test on the Core Ultra 7 155H / 32GB unit (Andrew Marc David). Speed is where takes split: the Core Ultra 7 155H is a bit ahead of an Apple M3 in Geekbench and Cinebench but well behind in graphics (PCWorld), gains over last year's 13th gen chip are small (Andrew Marc David), and the 8GB Core Ultra 5 model could not load Red Dead Redemption 2 (Lon.TV). Battery also depends on load, with three and a half hours under high load at full brightness on the Core Ultra 7 155H / 32GB model (PCWorld), and fans get loud in performance modes, reaching 49 dB on that same chip and RAM combination (Andrew Marc David).

highlights.text: fans get loud in performance modes

paras: Reviewers praise the 1.5 kg body, the 3K 120Hz OLED and integrated graphics that beat Snapdragon X Elite laptops in games (Max Tech, The Verge), though the HX 370 model's screen measured a dim 357 nits (Tom's Hardware) and Tech Guy Beau calls the screen door effect a deal breaker. Battery is where takes split: the HX 370 version with 32GB lasted 11 hours 35 minutes in a browsing test and trailed Arm laptops (Tom's Hardware), and drained about twice as fast as a MacBook Air 15 M2 in heavy editing (Ben G Kaiser), while the Ryzen AI 9 365 model logged 11 hours 52 minutes in office use (Andrew Marc David). Warmth under load also comes up, including on the 365 model (Danny Winget, MistaCat_).

Reviewers who like it, including Tom's Hardware, Techaeris and GregglesTV, praise the thin aluminum build, the OLED and the battery life, which reached 13 hours 27 minutes in Tom's Hardware's test of the 64GB Snapdragon X2 Elite model, though Just Josh measured around 10 hours at 300 nits. Mixed takes come from heat, ports and price: Just Josh measured 40° C near the top of the keyboard in light use and found it burning hot under pure CPU load, while Tom's Hardware called the $2,879.99 price of its review unit excessive and Tom's Guide called its unit's price egregious. On comparisons, the Intel Panther Lake version is the pick for gaming and legacy x86 software (Techaeris), the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x has a better keyboard and cooler feel (Just Josh), and the MacBook Air is cheaper and still recommended for anyone undecided between macOS and Windows (WIRED).

highlights.text: burning hot under pure CPU load

paras: Reviewers mostly praise the silent fanless build, the bright OLED screen and the keyboard, and it suits people content to stay on ChromeOS. Battery results on the Kompanio Ultra 910 16GB models range from about 8 hours in MergeDroid's estimate to over 15 hours in Notebookcheck's Wi-Fi test, and the limited ports, with no HDMI, draw repeated complaints. Price is where reviewers hesitate, with Tom's Guide calling $649 steep and noting that a similarly priced Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3x runs full Windows but has a much worse display (Tom's Guide), while TechRadar finds the Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7441 sharper and more versatile (TechRadar).

Reviewers mostly suit it to gamers who want strong performance at mid-range money, praising the keyboard and the cooling, while Lon.TV and Notebookcheck note there is no Thunderbolt. Battery results split by config: the Core i7-14650HX and RTX 4060 model with a 240Hz panel lasted 7 hours 24 minutes of web browsing (Notebookcheck), but the Core i9-14900HX and RTX 4060 model managed 3 hours 36 minutes (Laptop Mag). The two mixed reviews are about price, with Jarrod'sTech finding it hard to justify against 2023 models and pointing to the Legion 7i for a thinner build (Jarrod'sTech), and Tom's Hardware FR calling it overpriced at 1949 euros and pointing to the Legion Pro 5i with RTX 4070 (Tom's Hardware FR).

Reviewers who tested the Core i9-14900HX and RTX 4070 version mostly praise its gaming and CPU speed, upgradeable RAM and bright 240Hz screen. Comparisons split on speed: it led the ROG Zephyrus G16 2024 in Cinebench and games (Jarrod'sTech), but gaming came out about the same as that laptop because of the 4070 power cap (Josh Craves Tech), and it trailed the MSI Vector 17 HX in every game test (PC Gamer). Battery is the clearest complaint, from under 2 hours unplugged (Mark Guim) to under 3 hours of playback (Technic-Ali), though Notebookcheck measured 7h 13min of Wi-Fi browsing on its 3.2K model.

Reviewers praise the keyboard, the OLED screen and the speed of the RTX 5070 Ti versions, which suit gamers who also edit video. Opinions split on the RTX 5070 with 8GB of VRAM, which Tech Guy Beau says to skip because of ray tracing limits, while Jon Rettinger found the RTX 5070 model quiet and capable for creative work and games. Against the AMD Legion Pro 5, the Intel chip peaks 5 to 10% higher in Cinebench but draws 30 to 40% more watts and runs louder (Tech Guy Beau), and Notebookcheck found Performance mode loud on the RTX 5070 Ti model.

highlights.text: speed of the RTX 5070 Ti versions

paras: Reviewers mostly suit it to gamers and creators who want top performance at a desk, praising the keyboard, the 240Hz screen and cooling that helps it hold speed. Mixed takes come from weight and battery, where the RTX 4080 version lasted about 2.75 hours at 240Hz in OWNorDisown's test and gave 45 minutes to an hour of heavy gaming for Mark Linsangan, while the RTX 4090 version managed about 6 hours of video playback in battery saver mode (Hardware Voyage). On comparisons, it was faster in every game than the Zephyrus G16 with a 115W RTX 4090 (Mark Linsangan) and beat the Asus ROG Strix Scar 16 in 1080p game runs (GamesRadar+), though Just Josh would pick the Alienware x16 R2 for its keyboard and cooler feel in gaming.

highlights.text: cooling that helps it hold speed
45 minutes to an hour of heavy gaming

paras: Reviewers who tested the Ryzen 7 8845HS and RTX 4060 version praise it as a low-priced gaming laptop with easy upgrades and Lenovo Vantage modes. Weight is close to the Legion 5 Slim and lighter than the Legion 5 Pro (Tech Guy Beau), the styling resembles the Legion 5 15 without looking cheap (Onur Binay), and the Intel LOQ 15IRX9 was cheaper at writing time while only the AMD model offers the 2560x1440 panel (TheHikaku). Mixed takes come from noise and memory: fans measured 54 dB in performance mode (Onur Binay) and 53 dB (TheHikaku), so Tech Guy Beau and TheHikaku prefer balanced mode, and TheHikaku found the single 16GB stick made a Premiere 4K export take 5 minutes 56 seconds against 3 minutes 47 seconds with a second stick.

Reviewers who liked it call it a cheap gaming laptop with a good keyboard, such as AdminPong, who saw about 140 fps with DLSS and frame generation on the RTX 5050 version, while Digit praised the speed of the Core i7-14700HX and RTX 5060 model but found the price hard to justify. Mixed takes come from price and the 100W GPU limit: Binosha Tech and Binosha - بینوشا both put the RTX 5060 version 10 to 15% below rival RTX 5060 laptops, with one pointing to a Legion 5 with RTX 4060 at almost the same price (Binosha Tech) and the other to the ASUS TUF (Binosha - بینوشا). Battery is the common complaint, with NotebookSPEC measuring 2 hours 16 minutes on the RTX 5050 model and suggesting the Ryzen 7 260 LOQ for longer runtime (NotebookSPEC).

highlights.text: cheap gaming laptop with a good keyboard
2 hours 16 minutes on the RTX 5050 model

paras: Reviewers mostly like it as a cheap, sturdy ThinkPad with a comfortable keyboard and room to upgrade RAM and SSDs, suited to office, school and budget buyers, though the screens measured show weak colour coverage. Battery results vary by config and test: the Core Ultra 7 155U model managed 9h 26min of WiFi browsing (Notebookcheck) but only 5 hours 36 minutes in the PCMark 10 battery test (XDA Developers), while the Ryzen 5 7535HS version ran nearly 19 hours of video and browsing but cut its CPU power after 30 to 45 minutes (TECHSETTER). Against its siblings, the Intel model is preferred over the AMD version this year because the AMD one uses a previous generation CPU (Tech Guy Beau), while the Ryzen 7 7735HS model's Radeon 680M scored almost 86 percent higher in 3DMark than the E14 Gen 5 AMD (Notebookcheck, German review).

highlights.text: room to upgrade RAM and SSDs

paras: Reviewers mostly pitch it as an office laptop and praise the keyboard, with Tech Guy Beau calling it a superb typing experience. The screen splits opinion by config: Tech Guy Beau liked the 1600p panel and Notebookcheck measured 410 nits on the WQHD option, while PCMag Australia called the 1920 by 1200 Intel model's screen dim and bland, and TechRadar measured 54% sRGB on its Ryzen 5 7530U unit. Battery runs from about 3.5 hours of general use on the Core i5-1335U model (How-To Geek) to over 11 hours on the Ryzen 7 7730U WQHD model (Notebookcheck), and the Acer TravelMate P4 TMP416-51-55KN offers similar performance with more modern ports (Notebookcheck).

It suits office and web work, with reviewers praising the keyboard and the port selection, including Ethernet, HDMI and a fast USB port. The screen is where takes split: Tech Guy Beau liked the optional 100% sRGB 1200p panel on the Ryzen 7 7735U model, while Notebookcheck measured 56.1% sRGB on the Ryzen 5 7535U unit and Saverio Cirillo cited 45% NTSC on the Core i5 125U one. The HP ProBook 445 G10 is cheaper and lighter but lacks USB4 and WWAN (Notebookcheck), and the Ryzen 5 7535U unit managed 12h 28min of web surfing, slightly less than the L14 Gen 4 (Notebookcheck).

highlights.text: praising the keyboard and the port selection

paras: Reviewers mostly suit it to editors, developers and other professionals who want a portable workstation, praising the keyboard and speakers, and Laptop Mag recorded 17 hours 23 minutes of web surfing on the Core Ultra 7 165H, RTX 1000 Ada IPS model. Performance is where takes split, as the RTX 4060 version holds about 60W in games against 80W on the Gen 6 (Mash IT) and runs hot and loud, while the 4060 model also drops the Gen 6's high-end GPU options (Notebookcheck).
